title: When the Text Is Silent: Memory Shortcuts and the Validity of LLM Annotation under Evidence Insufficiency
abstract: arXiv:2611.02273v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to annotate text for social science research, content moderation, and training data. Their broad knowledge of real-world entities raises a concern: when labeling a text, do they rely on its evidence or substitute what they already know? We call this behavior a memory shortcut and examine when it emerges, what amplifies it, and how to mitigate it. Using 995 widely recognized public figures and four matched control names per figure, we construct counterfactual texts that separate textual evidence from prior knowledge, and evaluate three commercial LLMs on 121,594 prompts each across five stages. We find a striking asymmetry. Although all models recognize nearly every figure, none follows memory over the text when the two conflict. translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被用于为社会科学研究、内容审核和训练数据标注文本。它们对现实世界实体的广泛知识引发了一个担忧：在标注文本时，它们是依赖文本中的证据，还是用已知知识替代？我们将这种行为称为“记忆捷径”，并研究它何时出现、什么因素会放大它、以及如何缓解它。我们使用995位广为人知的公众人物以及每位人物对应的四个匹配对照名称，构建了将文本证据与先验知识分离的反事实文本，并在五个阶段中对三个商业大语言模型各进行了121,594次提示评估。我们发现了一种显著的不对称性：尽管所有模型几乎都能识别每一位人物，但当文本与记忆冲突时，没有任何模型会遵循记忆而非文本。相反，捷径是在证据缺失时出现的：对于其中一个模型，著名名字使“记忆出的”职业、年龄和国家的比例提高了17.0、14.9和
tldr: 该研究构建了分离文本证据与先验知识的反事实文本，发现大语言模型在文本与记忆冲突时不会用记忆覆盖文本，但当文本证据缺失时会依赖对知名人物的先验记忆产生“记忆捷径”，从而影响LLM标注的有效性。
en_tdlr: This study constructs counterfactual texts that separate textual evidence from prior knowledge, finding that LLMs never follow memory over text when the two conflict, but memory shortcuts emerge when evidence is absent, as famous names trigger reliance on prior knowledge and compromise the validity of LLM annotation.
